    <meta name="description" content="Whakatāne District Council | 2,702 followers on LinkedIn. We serve Whakatāne, Ōhope, Tāneatua, Edgecumbe, Matatā, Murupara and other communities throughout the Whakatāne District | PURPOSE

Great services, excellent delivery

• We provide governance, leadership and advocacy for the people of the District;

• We provide quality infrastructure including community facilities, roads, sewerage, water and stormwater systems;

• We deliver regulatory services focused on public health, safety and wellbeing;

• We develop long-term plans and strategies to provide a framework for change and sustainable development in our community.

VISION

To be respected by our community for the provision and delivery of excellent services which ensure that both present and future generations have:

• A quality environment in which to enjoy our great climate;

• A respect for and pride in our history;

• A community that is friendly and caring;

• A place that is known to be the best to live, work and play in and where people want to come.">

Best kept out of sight, out of mind. But not for the GT Civil crew doing the hard mahi down here at Buddle Street 👀👏🏽\n\nMost of us don’t give wastewater a second thought, but every shower, load of washing and toilet flush relies on a network of underground pipes, tanks and pump stations working behind the scenes to keep things moving.\n\nWe’re making good progress on the new Buddle Street Wastewater Pump Station, which will help improve reliability, increase capacity and support future growth for Whakatāne.\n\nAround 90% of it will end up underground, doing its job quietly in the background, exactly where most people prefer their wastewater to be 💩💦🙌🏽\n\nRead more: https://lnkd.in/e6Yc63Uy","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/whakatane-district-council_wastewater-best-kept-out-of-sight-out-of-activity-7482195537706954752-G1wY"},{"@context":"http://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"Whakatāne District Council","url":"https://nz.linkedin.com/company/whakatane-district-council"},"datePublished":"2026-06-30T00:00:02.813Z","mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/whakatane-district-council_after-47-years-with-whakat%C4%81ne-district-council-activity-7477511230723702784-sRHO","text":"After 47 years with Whakatāne District Council, and more than 50 years in local government, Jeff Farrell is leaving behind an extraordinary legacy as he transitions towards retirement.\n\nJeff’s career has spanned several areas of local government - environmental health, building, liquor licensing, resource management, natural hazards, climate change adaptation and plenty more in between. Across those years, he has led teams, mentored colleagues, shared his deep knowledge and helped shape some of the district’s most complex and important work.\n\nHe has helped influence national building regulation standards, developed practices for natural hazard and rapid building assessments following significant events, and played a key role in challenging natural hazard responses.\n\nOne of Jeff’s most significant contributions was leading the managed retreat programme following the 2005 debris flow at the Awatarariki fanhead in Matatā. It was the first time a managed retreat programme had been successfully carried out in New Zealand and became a nationally recognised example of how difficult, complex and deeply human adaptation work can be done.\n\nMost recently, Jeff has been a key figure in developing the Council’s Adaptation Explorer tool, helping staff and the public better understand climate change risks across the district.\n\nIn 2022, Jeff received the Local Government New Zealand Award for Excellence in Local Government, a rare recognition for a staff member and a clear reflection of the respect he has earned from peers across the sector.\nIt’s hard to capture 47 years of service in one post.\n\nJeff’s contribution sits in the projects he has led, the people he has guided, the standards he has helped shape and the knowledge he has generously passed on.\n\nNgā mihi nui, Jeff. Thank you for your service, your leadership and your lasting contribution to Whakatāne District Council and our communities. He's the one who wears the important white vest 😍 \n\nCalm under pressure, strategic, and someone who knows the ropes, Nicholas is focused on what matters most. He brings clarity when information is changing fast, helps set priorities, and pulls the team together to keep things moving forward.\n\nI orea te tuatara ka patu ki waho.\nA problem is solved by continuing to find solutions.\n\nThis whakataukī reflects the way emergencies are managed, through adaptability, creative thinking and perseverance. It speaks to Nicholas’s approach as Local Duty Controller, staying focused, adjusting as situations evolve, and working through challenges as they arise 🙌 \n\nDuring Cyclone Vaianu, around 40 staff worked inside the Emergency Operations Centre, supported by frontline teams like roading and waters out on the ground doing critical mahi in tough conditions. As Local Duty Controller, Nicholas stood at the centre of that response, supported by the skill, experience and commitment of the wider team working together to help guide the Whakatāne District through a challenging event.\n\nKa pai tō mahi, Nicholas. Do not lift the paddle out of unison or our canoe will never reach the shore.”\n\nJohn works hard to ensure our district is well prepared for any emergencies that might happen, like earthquakes, tsunami, or flooding. His calm, wise and knowledgeable skills help to steer the Emergency Management waka and keep us all safe and working together in unison 🛶 \n\nThank you, John, for having our district’s back and always thinking five steps ahead 💛 ","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/whakatane-district-council_faces-behind-the-mahi-meet-john-emergency-activity-7473471258916003840-TF50"},{"@context":"http://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"Whakatāne District Council","url":"https://nz.linkedin.com/company/whakatane-district-council"},"datePublished":"2026-06-17T00:11:26.795Z","headline":"","mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/whakatane-district-council_trigger-warning-something-weird-comes-out-activity-7472803057341485056-GAtY","text":"*TRIGGER WARNING: SOMETHING WEIRD COMES OUT OF PIPE*\n\nIntroducing the unsung hero under your feet: watermains 💛 \n\nAll over the district you’ll often find little mini holes along the side of the road as we upgrade the drinking water pipes, we call this mahi watermains renewals. These humble blue pipes are our lifeline to safe drinking water, and we’d be pretty parched without them 🥵 \n\n*In case you were wondering, after pigging, there are more steps completed to fully sterilise the pipe, and test it, before it is put into action 💦 ","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/whakatane-district-council_trigger-warning-something-weird-comes-out-activity-7472803057341485056-GAtY"},{"@context":"http://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"Whakatāne District Council","url":"https://nz.linkedin.com/company/whakatane-district-council"},"datePublished":"2026-06-15T23:34:22.106Z","mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/whakatane-district-council_faces-behind-the-mahi-meet-neal-our-team-activity-7472431338353143808-ZPiZ","text":"Faces behind the mahi – meet Neal, our Team Leader for water and wastewater treatment, and if anyone knows water, it’s him. He knows it like the back of his hand, honestly, it feels like he was born for the job!\n\nFrom turning storm-affected river water into clear, safe drinking water, to making sure everything flows where it should behind the scenes, Neal’s across it all. He’s also brilliant at explaining it, whether that’s to colleagues or school groups visiting the plant, he makes complex stuff simple and easy to understand.\n\nWhen things get tough, Neal’s out there braving the elements, keeping things running so water keeps flowing and flushing across the Whakatāne District.\n\nNeal started with us in October 1979 – that’s over 45 years of knowledge. He’s seen it all and fixed it all, and we’re incredibly lucky to have him and everything he brings to looking after water services for the Whakatāne District.\n\nBy day (and sometimes night), Neal is all about water. By night, he continues mahi on his farm, and he’s an avid off-road motorbike lover and regularly treks across outback NZ, not to mention a volunteer fire fighter! 💦🔥 \n\nMost of us just turn on the tap and don’t think twice. Neal is one of the people making that possible, keeping us hydrated and doing his part to help keep us regular. He’s one of our good sorts. And we’re so grateful to work with this cheeky lad 💛💩🚰 ","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/whakatane-district-council_faces-behind-the-mahi-meet-neal-our-team-activity-7472431338353143808-ZPiZ"},{"@context":"http://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"Whakatāne District Council","url":"https://nz.linkedin.com/company/whakatane-district-council"},"datePublished":"2026-06-04T22:30:18.576Z","mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/whakatane-district-council_awakeri-structure-plan-workshop-2-update-activity-7468428950898098176-ZvhF","text":"🌱 Awakeri Structure Plan: Workshop #2 update \n\nThe second Awakeri Community Reference Group workshop was held on Wednesday, 20 May, with around 25 locals coming along to help test early ideas for the draft Awakeri Structure Plan. \n\nAnd test them they did. 👀 \n\nUsing maps and planning layers, the group looked at how things like flooding, soil types, waterways, roads, community facilities and open spaces could shape future growth in Awakeri. \n\nThere were some great ideas on the table, including: \n\n🚶 better walking and cycling links \n🌿 restoring waterways and creating more natural public spaces \n🏡 protecting the village feel of Awakeri \n🚗 making the state highway feel safer and less like a racetrack \n🏘️ thinking carefully about where new homes could go \n\nBut it definitely wasn’t all “yay growth, let’s go”. The group also raised some very real concerns about flooding, stormwater, drainage, school capacity, highway safety, peat soils, heavy vehicles and the cost of infrastructure. \nWhich is exactly the point of these workshops. \n\nThe Structure Plan is still being developed, and no decisions have been made. This stage is about testing ideas early, asking questions, and ensuring local knowledge is part of the process. \n\nA big thank you to everyone who has shared their time and honest feedback so far. \n\nPlanning for growth is never simple, but it is much better when the people who know the place best are part of the kōrero. 🙌 \n\nRead the full summary 👉🏼 https://lnkd.in/eBuNGcWd","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/whakatane-district-council_awakeri-structure-plan-workshop-2-update-activity-7468428950898098176-ZvhF"},{"@context":"http://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"Whakatāne Council","url":"https://nz.linkedin.com/company/whakatane-district-council"},"datePublished":"2026-06-02T00:52:09.332Z","mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/whakatane-district-council_more-homes-more-pressure-more-planning-activity-7467377483991142401-p2lp","text":"More homes, more pressure, more planning needed. 🏡\n\nWhakatāne District is growing and changing, so we need to plan carefully for where growth happens, what infrastructure is needed 🛣️ and how we protect the things that make our communities great. 🌿\n\nIn comes our Local Growth Strategy, adopted last week at the Strategy and Policy Committee meeting! 🙌\n\nIt’s a 30-year plan to help guide how and where our district grows over time.\n\nIt looks at the big stuff:\n\n🏘️ housing\n🚗 roads and infrastructure\n🌊 natural hazards and resilience\n🌿 the environment\n🤝 working with iwi and hapū\n🏡 keeping our communities liveable and connected\n\nAnd just to be clear, this doesn’t mean diggers are turning up tomorrow. 🚜😅\n\nThe strategy doesn’t rezone land, approve development or lock in funding decisions.\n\nWhat it does do is give Council a clearer roadmap for future planning, including structure plans like the one now underway for Awakeri. 🗺️\n\nBecause growth is coming, and it’s much     <p class="attributed-text-segment-list__content text-color-text !text-sm whitespace-pre-wrap break-words
        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">After 47 years with Whakatāne District Council, and more than 50 years in local government, Jeff Farrell is leaving behind an extraordinary legacy as he transitions towards retirement.

Jeff’s career has spanned several areas of local government - environmental health, building, liquor licensing, resource management, natural hazards, climate change adaptation and plenty more in between. Across those years, he has led teams, mentored colleagues, shared his deep knowledge and helped shape some of the district’s most complex and important work.

He has helped influence national building regulation standards, developed practices for natural hazard and rapid building assessments following significant events, and played a key role in challenging natural hazard responses.

One of Jeff’s most significant contributions was leading the managed retreat programme following the 2005 debris flow at the Awatarariki fanhead in Matatā. It was the first time a managed retreat programme had been successfully carried out in New Zealand and became a nationally recognised example of how difficult, complex and deeply human adaptation work can be done.

Most recently, Jeff has been a key figure in developing the Council’s Adaptation Explorer tool, helping staff and the public better understand climate change risks across the district.

In 2022, Jeff received the Local Government New Zealand Award for Excellence in Local Government, a rare recognition for a staff member and a clear reflection of the respect he has earned from peers across the sector.
It’s hard to capture 47 years of service in one post.

Jeff’s contribution sits in the projects he has led, the people he has guided, the standards he has helped shape and the knowledge he has generously passed on.

Ngā mihi nui, Jeff. Thank you for your service, your leadership and your lasting contribution to Whakatāne District Council and our communities. </p>

    <p class="attributed-text-segment-list__content text-color-text !text-sm whitespace-pre-wrap break-words
        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">Faces behind the mahi – meet Neal, our Team Leader for water and wastewater treatment, and if anyone knows water, it’s him. He knows it like the back of his hand, honestly, it feels like he was born for the job!

From turning storm-affected river water into clear, safe drinking water, to making sure everything flows where it should behind the scenes, Neal’s across it all. He’s also brilliant at explaining it, whether that’s to colleagues or school groups visiting the plant, he makes complex stuff simple and easy to understand.

When things get tough, Neal’s out there braving the elements, keeping things running so water keeps flowing and flushing across the Whakatāne District.

Neal started with us in October 1979 – that’s over 45 years of knowledge. He’s seen it all and fixed it all, and we’re incredibly lucky to have him and everything he brings to looking after water services for the Whakatāne District.

By day (and sometimes night), Neal is all about water. By night, he continues mahi on his farm, and he’s an avid off-road motorbike lover and regularly treks across outback NZ, not to mention a volunteer fire fighter! 💦🔥 

Most of us just turn on the tap and don’t think twice. Neal is one of the people making that possible, keeping us hydrated and doing his part to help keep us regular. He’s one of our good sorts. And we’re so grateful to work with this cheeky lad 💛💩🚰 </p>

    <p class="attributed-text-segment-list__content text-color-text !text-sm whitespace-pre-wrap break-words
        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">🌱 Awakeri Structure Plan: Workshop #2 update 

The second Awakeri Community Reference Group workshop was held on Wednesday, 20 May, with around 25 locals coming along to help test early ideas for the draft Awakeri Structure Plan. 

And test them they did. 👀 

Using maps and planning layers, the group looked at how things like flooding, soil types, waterways, roads, community facilities and open spaces could shape future growth in Awakeri. 

There were some great ideas on the table, including: 

🚶 better walking and cycling links 
🌿 restoring waterways and creating more natural public spaces 
🏡 protecting the village feel of Awakeri 
🚗 making the state highway feel safer and less like a racetrack 
🏘️ thinking carefully about where new homes could go 

But it definitely wasn’t all “yay growth, let’s go”. The group also raised some very real concerns about flooding, stormwater, drainage, school capacity, highway safety, peat soils, heavy vehicles and the cost of infrastructure. 
Which is exactly the point of these workshops. 

The Structure Plan is still being developed, and no decisions have been made. This stage is about testing ideas early, asking questions, and ensuring local knowledge is part of the process. 

A big thank you to everyone who has shared their time and honest feedback so far. 

Planning for growth is never simple, but it is much better when the people who know the place best are part of the kōrero. 🙌

    <p class="attributed-text-segment-list__content text-color-text !text-sm whitespace-pre-wrap break-words
        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">More homes, more pressure, more planning needed. 🏡

Whakatāne District is growing and changing, so we need to plan carefully for where growth happens, what infrastructure is needed 🛣️ and how we protect the things that make our communities great. 🌿

In comes our Local Growth Strategy, adopted last week at the Strategy and Policy Committee meeting! 🙌

It’s a 30-year plan to help guide how and where our district grows over time.

It looks at the big stuff:

🏘️ housing
🚗 roads and infrastructure
🌊 natural hazards and resilience
🌿 the environment
🤝 working with iwi and hapū
🏡 keeping our communities liveable and connected

And just to be clear, this doesn’t mean diggers are turning up tomorrow. 🚜😅

The strategy doesn’t rezone land, approve development or lock in funding decisions.

What it does do is give Council a clearer roadmap for future planning, including structure plans like the one now underway for Awakeri. 🗺️

Because growth is coming, and it’s much better to plan for it properly than cross our fingers and hope the roads, pipes and houses magically sort themselves out. 🤞🏽🏘️🚰
